title: Asynchronous cash closes constrain which scheduled releases can affect a given weekly Friday endpoint
motivation: Nov20 10:00 EST BLS state labor release occurs after Friday Nikkei/KOSPI/CSI300 cash closes but before Friday STOXX600/S&P500/Nasdaq100 cash closes. Nov19 nominal Dallas WEI 10:30 CST coincides with European cash-close proxy. Existing common-shock model uses undated weeklong shocks.
prediction_hypothesis: Holding information cutoff, scenario probabilities, volatility assumptions, interval definitions and target cohorts fixed, a pre-registered instrument-specific event-exposure mask might improve held-out risk Brier/interval calibration versus uniformly applied release shocks over at least 26 scored weekly cohorts.
test_protocol: Require exact release time, observed publication time when recorded, each venue last cash close and its actual calendar; mark coincident clocks as unavailable or sensitivity bands.
Before each week's future outcomes, freeze paired uniform-shock vs time-gated-shock forecasts for the exact same market and risk targets, all event effect sizes, and versioned code.
Keep 26 weekly paired cohorts without post-hoc exclusions; explicitly track inaccessible or revised releases, source-vintage differences and share of omitted events.
Compare Brier per target, 50/90 interval scores per unit and coverage, block bootstrap by week; allow null result, do not adjust past forecasts.
If event effects cannot be estimated ex-ante, retain a named synthetic stress only and do not score it as a prediction.
falsification: With frozen paired valid cohorts, masked variant shows no skill benefit or reduced coverage/skill after accounting for missingness and publication-time uncertainty.
warning: These baseline probabilities and hypothetical stress outcomes are model-calculated; no observed Nov16-Nov20 market outcomes and no causal effect estimate.
date_policy: This is registered after Saturday Nov14 noon and cannot be credited as a Nov14 12:00 frozen A/B/C forecast.
